docs.title: API / Transactional
docs.text: Method Endpoint Description POST /api/tx Send transactional messages

docs.title: POST /api/tx
docs.text: Allows sending transactional messages to one or more subscribers via a preconfigured transactional template.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Required Description subscriber_email string Email of the subscriber. Can substitute with subscriber_id. subscriber_id number Subscriber's ID can substitute with subscriber_email. subscriber_emails string[] Multiple subscriber emails as alternative to subscriber_email. subscriber_ids number[] Multiple subscriber IDs as an alternative to subscriber_id. subscriber_mode string Subscriber lookup mode: default, fallback, or external template_id number Yes ID of the transactional template to be used for the message. from_email string Optional sender email. subject string Optional subject. If empty, the subject defined on the template is used data JSON Optional nested JSON map. Available in the template as {{ .Tx.Data.* }}. headers JSON[] Optional array of email headers. messenger string Messenger to send the message. Default is email. content_type string Email format options include html, markdown, and plain. altbody string Optional alternate plaintext body for multipart HTML emails.

docs.title: Subscriber modes
docs.text:
The subscriber_mode parameter controls how the recipients (subscribers or non-subscriber recipients) are resolved.

Mode Description default Recipients must exist as subscribers in the database. Pass either subscriber_emails or subscriber_ids. fallback Only accepts subscriber_emails and looks up subscribers in the database. If not found, sends the message to the e-mail anyway. In the template, apart from {{ .Subscriber.Email }}, other subscriber fields such as .Name. will be empty. Use {{ Tx.Data.* }} instead. external Sends to the given subscriber_emails without subscriber lookup in the database. In the template, apart from {{ .Subscriber.Email }}, other subscriber fields such as .Name. will be empty. Use {{ Tx.Data.* }} instead.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
curl -u "api_user:token" "http://localhost:9000/api/tx" -X POST \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
     --data-binary @- << EOF
    {
        "subscriber_email": "user@test.com",
        "template_id": 2,
        "data": {"order_id": "1234", "date": "2022-07-30", "items": [1, 2, 3]},
        "content_type": "html"
    }
EOF

docs.title: Example response
docs.text:
{
    "data": true
}

docs.title: Example with external mode
docs.text:
Send to arbitrary email addresses without requiring them to be subscribers:

curl -u "api_user:token" "http://localhost:9000/api/tx" -X POST \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
     --data-binary @- << EOF
    {
        "subscriber_mode": "external",
        "subscriber_emails": ["recipient@example.com"],
        "template_id": 2,
        "data": {"name": "John", "order_id": "1234"},
        "content_type": "html"
    }
EOF

In the template, use {{ .Tx.Data.name }}, {{ .Tx.Data.order_id }}, etc. to access the data.

docs.title: File Attachments
docs.text:
To include file attachments in a transactional message, use the multipart/form-data Content-Type. Use data param for the parameters described above as a JSON object. Include any number of attachments via the file param.

curl -u "api_user:token" "http://localhost:9000/api/tx" -X POST \
-F 'data=\"{
    \"subscriber_email\": \"user@test.com\",
    \"template_id\": 4
}"' \
-F 'file=@"/path/to/attachment.pdf"' \
-F 'file=@"/path/to/attachment2.pdf"'

docs.title: Developers
docs.text:
The Developers area of the sidebar is for connecting your own systems to listnun: sending transactional email (receipts, password resets, alerts) from your code, and hearing back what happened to it.

Page What it's for Overview A four-step quickstart, plus today's sending numbers and recent messages. API keys Credentials for your code, each limited to the scopes it needs. See API keys. Email templates The transactional templates your code sends. See Transactional email. Send test Send a transactional template from the browser, with sample data, and copy the matching curl command. Message log Every transactional message: who it went to, its status, and the exact payload. Email branding Your logo for transactional emails, including a dark-mode version. See Email branding. Webhooks Endpoints listnun calls when a message is sent, delivered, bounces or fails. See Webhooks.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Developers › Overview walks you through four steps and ticks each one off as you go:

  1. Create an API key with the tx:send scope under Developers › API keys, one per service. Copy the secret: it's shown once, so keep it in your secrets manager.
  2. Pick a transactional template under Developers › Email templates, or create one. Note its ID.

  3. Send a test from your code. The Overview shows the call in curl, Node, Python and Go, already filled in with your workspace's address, your key's name, your template's ID and its sample data. The examples read the secret from a LISTNUN_API_KEY environment variable and use HTTP Basic auth (key name as the username, secret as the password):

    curlNodePythonGo 
    curl -X POST https://yourcompany.listnun.app/api/tx \
  -u "my-service:$LISTNUN_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "subscriber_email": "ada@example.com",
    "template_id": 3,
    "data": {"order_id": "1042", "total": "$25.00"}
  }'

    const auth = Buffer.from(
  `my-service:${process.env.LISTNUN_API_KEY}`,
).toString("base64");

await fetch("https://yourcompany.listnun.app/api/tx", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    "Authorization": `Basic ${auth}`,
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    subscriber_email: "ada@example.com",
    template_id: 3,
    data: { order_id: "1042", total: "$25.00" },
  }),
});

    import os, requests

requests.post(
    "https://yourcompany.listnun.app/api/tx",
    auth=("my-service", os.environ["LISTNUN_API_KEY"]),
    json={
        "subscriber_email": "ada@example.com",
        "template_id": 3,
        "data": {"order_id": "1042", "total": "$25.00"},
    },
    timeout=10,
).raise_for_status()

    body := strings.NewReader(`{
  "subscriber_email": "ada@example.com",
  "template_id": 3,
  "data": {"order_id": "1042", "total": "$25.00"}
}`)
req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://yourcompany.listnun.app/api/tx", body)
req.SetBasicAuth("my-service", os.Getenv("LISTNUN_API_KEY"))
req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)

    The Authorization: token my-service:<secret> header works too. See Auth.

  4. Check the log under Developers › Message log. The message appears within seconds, with a timeline from accepted to delivered or bounced.

By default the recipient must already be a subscriber in your workspace, or the call fails with HTTP 400. To email anyone, for example receipts to guest customers, add "subscriber_mode": "external". See the Transactional API reference.

docs.title: Let an AI assistant write it
docs.text:
The AI prompt tab, next to the code tabs, gives you a prompt instead of code. Paste it into Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or Copilot inside your project and it writes the integration in your own language and framework.

The prompt is filled in with your workspace's address, key name, template ID and the template's variables. It also tells the assistant to:

  • keep the key on the server, read from LISTNUN_API_KEY, never in browser code,
  • use subscriber_mode when the recipients aren't subscribers,
  • retry only on HTTP 429 and 5xx, with backoff, and log 400s instead of retrying,
  • use a 10-second timeout and wrap the call in one reusable function.

Review what the assistant writes like any other code before you ship it.

docs.title: The rest of the API
docs.text:
Everything you can do in the app can also be done through the REST API: lists, subscribers, campaigns, templates, media, bounces and more. See the API introduction and the reference pages under API.

Template syntax for both campaigns and transactional email is in the Templating reference.

docs.title: API keys
docs.text: An API key lets your code call the listnun API. Create one per service (your shop, your app's backend, a sync job) under Developers › API keys, so you can see where calls come from and revoke one without touching the others.

docs.title: Creating a key
docs.text:
Click Create API key, give it a name, and tick its scopes. Names are 2–63 characters of lowercase letters, numbers, dots, dashes and underscores, starting with a letter or number, such as shop-backend; the name is also what you authenticate with. listnun shows the secret once; store it in your secrets manager straight away. After that, only its last four characters are shown.

Secrets start with lnk_live_, so they're easy to spot if one leaks into a log or a repository.

Copy your secret now This is the only time it's shown. Store it in your secrets manager. lnk_live_8f2c1d6b0e4a9f37c5b2e8d1a6f0c3b7Copy shop-backendlnk_live_…c3b7tx:sendLast used 2 minutes agoActive crm-synclnk_live_…91aesubscribers:readNot used yetActive old-mailerlnk_live_…07d2tx:sendLast used 3 months agoRevoked

Developers › API keys, just after creating a key.

docs.title: Scopes
docs.text:
A key can only do what its scopes allow. It has no other permissions, whatever its creator can do.

Scope Allows tx:send Sending transactional email (POST /api/tx) and resending logged messages. tx:logs Reading the message log and sending stats. subscribers:read Reading subscribers. subscribers:manage Adding, updating, unsubscribing and deleting subscribers, and changing their lists. Adds lists:manage. subscribers:import Importing subscribers in bulk. Adds lists:manage. lists:read Reading lists. lists:manage Creating, editing and deleting lists. Adds lists:read. campaigns:read Reading campaigns and their analytics. Adds lists:read. campaigns:manage Creating, editing, scheduling, sending, pausing and deleting campaigns. Adds campaigns:read. templates:read / templates:manage Reading templates / creating, editing and deleting them. media:read / media:manage Reading uploaded media / uploading and deleting it. bounces:read / bounces:manage Reading bounces / deleting them and blocklisting bounced subscribers. keys:manage Listing, creating, rotating and revoking API keys. webhooks:manage Managing webhook endpoints and deliveries.

Give each key the fewest scopes it needs. A service that only sends receipts needs just tx:send.

docs.title: Authenticating
docs.text:
Send the key's name and secret in the Authorization header:

curl https://yourcompany.listnun.app/api/developers/messages \
  -H "Authorization: token my-service:lnk_live_…"

HTTP Basic auth with the same pair also works: curl -u "my-service:lnk_live_…" ….

A key belongs to one workspace and only works on that workspace's address.

docs.title: Rotating
docs.text: Rotate generates a new secret and shows it once. The previous secret keeps working for 24 hours, so you can deploy the new one without downtime. After that, only the new secret works.

docs.title: Revoking and deleting
docs.text:
Revoke stops a key working immediately, but keeps it in the list for your records. Delete removes it completely.

The list shows when each key was last used, which helps you find keys nothing uses any more.

docs.title: Keys migrated from API users
docs.text:
Older workspaces used "API users" (a username and token) instead of keys. Each one has been turned into a key with matching scopes, and its old username:token pair keeps working until you're ready to switch:

  1. Rotate the migrated key to get a real lnk_live_… secret. Until you do, it shows "No key secret yet".
  2. Update your code to use the key's name and new secret.
  3. Choose Disable old token from the key's menu. The old pair stops working.

docs.title: Email branding
docs.text:
Developers › Email branding sets the logo your transactional emails show.

  • Logo: upload or pick an image from your media library.
  • Dark-mode logo (optional): shown by email apps in dark mode. Without one, your logo sits on a white tile in dark mode so it stays readable.
  • Width, alignment and an optional link for the logo.

The preview shows the result in light and dark mode.

docs.title: Using it in templates
docs.text:
Put this where the logo should go in a transactional template:

{{ template "brand-logo" . }}

It renders nothing until a logo is set, so it's safe in every template. To lay the logo out your own way, define your own brand-logo block in the template and it replaces the built-in one.

Campaign templates don't use branding. Put your logo straight into the campaign template's HTML instead.

docs.title: Transactional email
docs.text: A transactional email goes to one person because something happened: an order, a sign-up, a password reset. You send it from your code with POST /api/tx and a transactional template. Unlike a campaign, it isn't sent to a list. By default the recipient must exist as a subscriber in your workspace (on any list or none); set subscriber_mode to fallback or external to send to any address. See the API reference.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
Create and edit transactional templates under Developers › Email templates. The editor shows a live preview next to the code, using sample data you can edit.

A transactional template has a subject and a body. Both can use:

  • {{ .Tx.Data.* }}: the data your code sends, e.g. {{ .Tx.Data.order_id }}.
  • {{ .Subscriber.* }}: the recipient, e.g. {{ .Subscriber.Name }}, when they're a subscriber.
  • {{ template "brand-logo" . }}: your workspace logo from Email branding.
{{ template "brand-logo" . }}
<p>Hi {{ .Subscriber.FirstName }},</p>
<p>Thanks for order #{{ .Tx.Data.order_id }}. Your total was {{ .Tx.Data.total }}.</p>

See the Templating reference for everything else you can use.

docs.title: Sending
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://yourcompany.listnun.app/api/tx \
  -H "Authorization: token my-service:lnk_live_…" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "subscriber_email": "ada@example.com",
    "template_id": 3,
    "data": {"order_id": "1042", "total": "$25.00"}
  }'

Your key needs the tx:send scope. The full list of fields (several recipients, sending to people who aren't subscribers, attachments, custom headers) is in the Transactional API reference.

To try a template without writing code, use Developers › Send test: pick the template, enter an address and sample data, and send. It also shows the curl command for the same request.

docs.title: The message log
docs.text:
Developers › Message log lists every transactional message, newest first. Filter by status, template, API key or date, or search by recipient or message ID. Open one to see its timeline and the exact data it was sent with.

Status Meaning queued Accepted, waiting to be sent. sent Handed to the mail server. delivered The receiving mail server accepted it (when your mail provider reports deliveries). bounced It couldn't be delivered. The bounce type is shown. failed listnun couldn't send it, for example because of a template error.

Resend sends a logged message again with the same data. Reading the log needs the tx:logs scope; resending needs tx:send.

To be told about these changes as they happen, set up webhooks.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text: A webhook tells your system what happened to a transactional message: listnun sends an HTTP POST to your endpoint each time a message is sent, delivered, bounces or fails. Set them up under Developers › Webhooks.

docs.title: Adding an endpoint
docs.text:
Click Add endpoint, enter its URL, and choose the events it should get. listnun shows the endpoint's signing secret (starting whsec_). Store it; you'll use it to check requests really come from listnun. You can Reveal it again later. Rotate secret replaces it, and deliveries are signed with the new one straight away, so update your endpoint at the same time.

Endpoints must be public https:// addresses. listnun refuses to call private, internal or loopback addresses.

Send test event sends a webhook.test event so you can check your endpoint before real traffic arrives.

A webhook endpoint with its recent deliveries.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: Event When message.sent The message was handed to the mail server. message.delivered The receiving server accepted it. message.bounced It bounced. message.failed listnun couldn't send it.

docs.title: The request
docs.text:
POST /your/endpoint HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
User-Agent: listnun-webhooks/1
Listnun-Event: message.bounced
Listnun-Delivery-Id: 7b1f…
Listnun-Signature: t=1761141600,v1=5f2c…

{
  "type": "message.bounced",
  "created_at": "2026-10-22T14:00:00Z",
  "data": {
    "message_id": "0c9e…",
    "template_id": 3,
    "recipient": "ada@example.com",
    "status": "bounced",
    "bounce": {"type": "hard", "detail": "550 5.1.1 user unknown"}
  }
}

data.bounce only appears on message.bounced, and data.error only on message.failed. Listnun-Delivery-Id is the same on every retry of a delivery, so you can use it to ignore duplicates.

docs.title: Checking the signature
docs.text:
Listnun-Signature is t=<unix seconds>,v1=<signature>, where the signature is the hex HMAC-SHA256 of <t>.<raw request body> using the endpoint's secret. To check a request:

  1. Split the header into t and v1.
  2. Compute HMAC-SHA256 of t + "." + body with your secret. Use the raw body bytes, before any JSON parsing.
  3. Compare it with v1 using a constant-time comparison.
  4. Reject requests whose t is more than a few minutes old, so a captured request can't be replayed.
import hashlib, hmac, time

def verify(secret: str, header: str, body: bytes, tolerance: int = 300) -> bool:
    parts = dict(p.split("=", 1) for p in header.split(","))
    t, sig = parts.get("t", ""), parts.get("v1", "")
    if not t.isdigit() or abs(time.time() - int(t)) > tolerance:
        return False
    expected = hmac.new(secret.encode(), f"{t}.".encode() + body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, sig)

import crypto from "node:crypto";

export function verify(secret, header, rawBody, tolerance = 300) {
  const parts = Object.fromEntries(header.split(",").map((p) => p.split("=")));
  const t = Number(parts.t);
  if (!t || Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - t) > tolerance) return false;
  const expected = crypto.createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${t}.${rawBody}`).digest("hex");
  return expected.length === parts.v1?.length &&
    crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(expected), Buffer.from(parts.v1));
}

docs.title: Responding and retries
docs.text:
Reply with any 2xx status within 10 seconds to accept a delivery. Do slow work after replying, not before.

Anything else, including a timeout or an error, counts as a failure, and listnun tries again after 4 minutes, 15 minutes, 1 hour, 4 hours, then every 6 hours. A delivery gets 8 attempts, about 23 hours in all, before it's marked failed and recorded in Settings › Activity log.

The endpoint's page shows recent deliveries with their status, response code and timing. Open one to see the payload and your endpoint's reply, or Retry it by hand.

docs.title: Writing and sending campaigns
docs.text: A campaign is an email you send to one or more lists. Campaigns › All campaigns opens an overview of what's sending, what's next and what's done; New campaign starts one.

docs.title: The campaigns overview
docs.text:
Section What it shows Paused banner One per paused campaign: how far it got and how many people are still waiting, with Review and Resume sending. Sending now Each running campaign's progress (sent of total), speed, time left and opens so far, refreshed every couple of seconds, with Pause and Live results, which opens the campaign in Analytics, refreshing every 30 seconds while it sends. Up next Scheduled campaigns by day, with their lists and audience. Drafts The latest three, with who edited them and when. All drafts shows the rest. Sent The latest four, with delivered, open rate and click rate. Show all sent and Compare in analytics go further.

To find any campaign, use Search campaigns. Search, All drafts and Show all sent open the full table of campaigns, with filters and bulk actions.

docs.title: The campaign editor
docs.text: The editor has four steps along the top: Settings, Content, Schedule and Review. Once the campaign is created you can move between them freely. Continue saves the step you're on and moves to the next.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Field Notes Campaign name For you and your team; subscribers don't see it. Subject The subject line. It can use template expressions, such as {{ .Subscriber.FirstName }}. From address Who it's from, written as Your Name <you@yourdomain.com>. Defaults to your workspace's address. Lists to send to One or more lists. Someone on several of them gets the email once, and blocklisted subscribers are never sent to. The Audience card shows how many subscribers that is. Tags Optional labels to organise your campaigns.

Advanced holds the messenger (normally email), custom email headers, and campaign attributes: a JSON object you can use in the content as {{ .Campaign.Attribs.* }}.

docs.title: Content
docs.text:
At the top, pick the Format and, for every format except Visual, the Template the content sits in (see Templates and media).

Format Best for Visual Building an email from blocks (headings, text, images, buttons, columns) without code. Start from scratch or Import visual template. Rich text Writing like in a word processor: headings, lists, links and images. Raw HTML Pasting in HTML from another tool, or hand-writing it. Markdown Plain writing that becomes simple HTML. Plain text No formatting at all.

Switching format converts what you've written, and some formatting may be lost, so listnun asks first.

Under the editor:

  • Attachments: click Add attachments to pick files from your media library. Each attached file is sent with every email, so keep them small.
  • Tracking: track link clicks, add tracking pixels and, if your workspace has it, track replies. See Tracking opens and clicks.
  • Plain-text version: for HTML formats, add a plain-text alternative for email apps that can't show HTML. Without one, those apps show nothing.

Preview (or F9) shows the email as a subscriber will see it, with sample data.

To personalise content, such as a subscriber's name, use template expressions like {{ .Subscriber.Name }}. See the Templating reference.

docs.title: Schedule
docs.text:
Choose Send now to start as soon as you confirm on the Review step, or Schedule for later and pick a date and time. Times are in your browser's time zone.

Archive publishes the campaign on your public archive page, a web page listing past campaigns people can browse. Set the URL slug and the sample subscriber data shown in place of real names. See Archives.

docs.title: Review
docs.text:
Spring saleDraftSend testStart campaign ✓Settings✓Content✓Schedule4Review ✓Subject and senderSpring sale: 20% off everything Acme <news@acme.com> ✓AudienceUp to 10,000 subscribers in Newsletter !Test emailSend yourself a test before you start it.Send test iTrackingLink clicks are tracked. iScheduleSends as soon as you start it.

The Review step, before a test has been sent.

A checklist of everything worth checking before sending:

  • Subject and sender are set.
  • Audience: how many people the campaign will go to, on which lists. Each person counts once, however many of the lists they're on, and only people it will actually be sent to count: not unsubscribed or blocklisted people, nor, for a regular campaign, people who haven't confirmed a double opt-in list.
  • Content isn't empty.
  • Unsubscribe link: whether the email has one. See The unsubscribe link.
  • Test email: amber until you've sent a test of exactly what's in the editor now. If you change the subject, content, attachments or tracking after testing, it turns amber again.
  • Tracking: whether link clicks are tracked, how many pixels, and whether replies are tracked.
  • Schedule.

Anything that needs attention has a button to fix it.

docs.title: The unsubscribe link
docs.text:
Gmail and Yahoo filter bulk email that has no visible unsubscribe link, so listnun warns you when a campaign doesn't have one. The link counts if the campaign's content or its template has {{ UnsubscribeURL }} or {{ ManageURL }}. A Visual campaign doesn't use a template, so for those only the content counts.

If it's missing, the Review step shows an amber Unsubscribe link check and the confirmation before sending says so. You can still send it. Add unsubscribe link adds a small footer with the link to the end of the content, in its own format. For a Visual campaign, it opens the email builder so you can add one to a footer block.

The template editor warns you when a campaign template has no unsubscribe link.

docs.title: Inbox check
docs.text:
The Inbox check on the Review step looks at the campaign as last saved for what commonly sends email to spam. It lists only what fails, each with what to do about it. Passing checks are folded away under Passing checks. None of them stop you sending, but the send confirmation tells you how many warnings there are.

Group Checks Content There's a plain-text version. The email is under Gmail's 102 KB limit, past which Gmail cuts it off and hides the rest, unsubscribe link included. It isn't mostly images. No links are empty, # or missing https://. No link shorteners. Subject It isn't empty or long enough to be cut off on phones (about 60 characters). It isn't mostly capitals. No repeated !! or $$. No phrases spam filters score. Sender The From address isn't on a free-mail domain such as gmail.com, which other servers can't send for. It's on the domain the workspace is set up to send from. Audience At most half the audience has gone 90 days without opening or clicking, the same rule as inactive cleanup. Over the last 30 days, the workspace's spam complaints stayed under 0.1% and hard bounces under 2% of its campaign email.

The complaint and bounce rates are only rated once the workspace has sent enough campaign email to measure them.

docs.title: Send a test
docs.text: Click Send test (on the Review step or at the top of the editor) and enter one or more email addresses. They must be subscribers in your workspace. The test uses what's in the editor, even if you haven't saved it, so you see exactly what will go out.

docs.title: Start
docs.text: Start campaign (or Schedule) asks you to confirm, with the number of subscribers it goes to. If you haven't sent a test of this version, the confirmation says so.

docs.title: While it sends
docs.text:
A running campaign shows on the overview under Sending now, where you can Pause it. A paused campaign gets a banner at the top; Resume sending picks up where it stopped, with the people still waiting.

In the full table of campaigns, each campaign's ⋯ menu can also Start, Schedule or Unschedule it, Cancel it, or open its Analytics. The copy button on any campaign clones it, a quick way to start a new campaign from an old one.

If your workspace uses email validation, starting is held back while a list is still being validated.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Campaigns › Analytics compares campaigns: how many people opened, clicked, bounced and, with Replies set up, replied, bounces split into hard and soft, and which links were clicked most. Pick the campaigns at the top. The totals and rates are each campaign's results all time, the same figures as on the Campaigns overview; the chart, links and bounce types follow the date range, which starts from the day the earliest campaign went out until you pick one.

Opens and clicks count people, once each per campaign, and rates are a share of delivered emails (sent, less those that bounced). Anyone who clicked counts as having opened, since many email apps block the image that records an open. Rates need Settings › Privacy › Individual subscriber tracking: without it each view and click is counted on its own, so only the counts are shown.

Opens are counted with a tracking image, which many email apps block until the reader allows images, so open counts are always a little low. Clicks are reliable. See Tracking opens and clicks.

docs.title: Replies
docs.text:
If your workspace has reply tracking, the Tracking card on the Content step has a Track replies switch. It's off by default. If you don't see it, reply tracking isn't set up for your workspace.

With it on, each email's Reply-To is a listnun reply address unique to that subscriber, so subscribers see that address when they reply. On listnun.app, you can put these addresses on your own domain, such as reply.yourcompany.com, under Reply domain on the workspace's page in the console. listnun records each reply and forwards it to the campaign's Reply-To address, or its From address if it has none, with the subscriber as the Reply-To. You can answer them straight from your own inbox.

Once the campaign starts sending, a Replies card on the campaign shows how many replies came in, who replied, and each reply. Out-of-office and other automatic replies are kept and marked Auto-reply, but aren't counted as replies.

docs.title: Importing subscribers
docs.text: Subscribers › Import adds many subscribers at once from a spreadsheet. It walks you through four steps, Upload, Match columns, Choose options and Review, and nothing is written until you click Start import on the last one.

docs.title: 1. Upload
docs.text:
Drop a .csv file on the upload area, or choose one from your computer. A .zip with one CSV inside also works. Files can be up to 50 MB, and they need a column of email addresses. Download a sample CSV shows the layout.

Column names can be anything: you match them up on the next step. Commas, semicolons, tabs and other separators are detected automatically.

Email,First name,City
ada@example.com,Ada,London
alan@example.com,Alan,

The uploaded file is kept for two hours while you finish the steps. If it expires, upload it again.

docs.title: 2. Match columns
docs.text:
Each column of your file is listed with its first few values and a guess at what it holds. For each, choose what to Save as:

Save as What happens Email The subscriber's address. One column must be this. Name The subscriber's name. Attribute Saved to the subscriber's attributes under the column's name, e.g. city. Any column you keep that isn't email or name is saved as an attribute. Attributes (JSON) A column that already holds a JSON object, such as {"city": "Harare", "plan": "pro"}. Don't import The column is ignored.

docs.title: 3. Choose options
docs.text: Question Choices What should happen to these people? Add them as subscribers, or Block these addresses: they never get email from this workspace and are unsubscribed from every list. Add them to The lists to add them to. Did they agree to hear from you? Only asked when a chosen list uses double opt-in. Not sure, ask them: they join once they click a confirmation email, which you send when the import is done. Yes, they opted in: they join straight away. Only pick this if you have their consent. People already here Shown when some addresses in the file are already subscribers. Leave them as they are only adds new people. Update their details replaces their names and attributes with the file's.

docs.title: 4. Review and import
docs.text:
Before anything is written, the Review step checks the whole file and tells you how many new subscribers there will be, how many people are already here (and whether they'll be updated or left alone), how many will need confirming, and which rows will be skipped and why. Click Start import to go ahead.

The import runs on the server, so you can leave the page and come back. While it runs you see its progress and how long is left. When it finishes you see exactly how many people were added and how many were already here.

Rows that weren't imported are listed with their row number in your spreadsheet, the value and the problem:

  • No email address
  • Not a valid email address
  • This email domain isn't allowed (see the domain lists in Privacy and consent)
  • Wrong number of columns

Download these rows saves them as a CSV, so you can fix them and import just those rows again.

If new people need to confirm a double opt-in list, nothing is sent automatically. The finished import offers Send confirmation emails, which sends them the confirmation email. People who were sent one, or added to a list, in the last 24 hours are skipped, so nobody gets two in a row.

Only one import runs at a time per workspace.

docs.title: Recent imports
docs.text: Finished imports are listed under Recent imports, with how many people each added or blocked and how many rows it skipped.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Large files are fine. Rows are written in batches, and the first ones show up in your subscriber list within a second or two.
  • Importing someone who's already on a list doesn't create a duplicate. An email address is one subscriber.
  • If your workspace uses email validation, imported addresses are checked in the background after the import.

docs.title: Lists
docs.text:
A list is a group of subscribers you send campaigns to. Open Lists › All lists to see them, with how many subscribers each has and how many are still waiting to confirm.

Each list has two settings that matter:

Setting Options Type Public lists can be added to signup forms and appear on subscribers' preferences page. Private lists are for your own segments; people can't join them themselves. Opt-in Single: people are subscribed straight away. Double: each new subscriber gets an email with a confirmation link, and campaigns only go to subscribers who confirmed.

Use double opt-in for lists people sign up to on your website. It keeps typos and fake addresses off your list and helps your emails reach inboxes.

Click a list to open its panel:

  • Growth: how many people joined and left each day over the last 30 days.
  • Campaigns: its latest campaigns, with how many people opened and clicked.
  • Signup form (public lists only): a link to a ready-made signup page for the list. See A quick link for one list.

From a list's ⋯ menu you can view its subscribers, import into it, or draft an opt-in campaign that asks its unconfirmed subscribers to confirm.

docs.title: People waiting to confirm
docs.text:
When people haven't confirmed a double opt-in subscription yet, a banner at the top of Lists says how many. Resend confirmation emails them the confirmation again. Anyone who was sent one, or joined a list, in the last day is skipped, so nobody gets two in a row. Only one resend runs at a time. You can also confirm people yourself.

Deleting a list doesn't delete its subscribers. They just stop being on that list.

docs.title: Signup forms
docs.text: Lists › Forms is where you keep your signup forms. Each form has its own lists, fields and wording, and you can share it three ways: as a hosted page, as HTML embedded in your website, or as a popup.

docs.title: Making a form
docs.text:
Click New form, then set:

Setting What it does Form name For your team. While the form is a draft, it also sets the hosted page's address. Lists people can join Only public lists can be added. With one list, people join it; with several, they tick the ones they want. The form tells you if any of them use double opt-in, in which case new people get a confirmation email before they're added. Fields Email always comes first and is required. Add Name, or up to 10 fields in all with Add a field: each extra field (e.g. City) is saved to the subscriber's attributes. Mark fields required or optional and drag them into order. Heading, Intro, Button label The text people see. After someone signs up The thank-you message. Left empty, people see a standard message, telling them to check their inbox when a list uses double opt-in. Bot protection Adds a Cloudflare Turnstile check. Set up Turnstile under Settings › Sign-in and security first. Every form also has a hidden trap field that catches simple bots.

The preview shows the form in light and dark themes. Save form keeps your changes.

docs.title: Publishing and sharing
docs.text:
A new form is a Draft: its page, embed and popup don't work until you click Publish form. A live form needs at least one list. While it's live, its address stays fixed even if you rename it, so links keep working. Unpublish turns it back into a draft: its page, embed and popup stop working, and renaming it then can change its address.

A live form's Share section has:

Way to share How Hosted page A page on your workspace's address, at /f/<form>. Link to it from social posts, email signatures or a QR code. Embed HTML to paste into your website where the form should go. It's unstyled, so it picks up your site's CSS, and it posts to the hosted page, which shows the result. Popup A <script> tag to add to your website's pages. The form pops up 8 seconds after a page opens, at most once a month per visitor.

docs.title: How a form is doing
docs.text:
Each form shows its signups in the last 30 days in the list of forms. Open a form to see, for the last 30 days, its Views, Signups, how many of those Confirmed, and how many submissions were Blocked by Turnstile.

Deleting a form stops its page, embeds and popup, and deletes its figures. People who signed up through it stay subscribed.

docs.title: A quick link for one list
docs.text: Every public list also has a ready-made signup link. Open the list and go to its Signup form tab to copy it. The link shows a simple form for just that list, with no setup needed. Customise the form takes you to Forms when you want more control.

docs.title: What subscribers see
docs.text:
Every campaign includes an unsubscribe link. Depending on your Settings › Privacy and consent, subscribers can also:

  • manage which of your public lists they're on,
  • download the data you hold about them,
  • delete their data.

People who unsubscribe land on a page where they can resubscribe if it was a mistake.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Workspace › Settings holds your workspace's configuration. Changes aren't saved until you click Save on the bar that appears at the bottom; Discard undoes them. If you try to leave with unsaved changes, listnun asks first.

On hosted listnun, some settings, such as mail servers and email validation, may be managed for you and shown read-only.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Settings opens on an overview with one card per area: Sending, Deliverability, Privacy and consent, Sign-in and security, File storage, Workspace and appearance, and Data and activity. Each card says what the area covers and links to its sections. A card only shows a status when something needs attention: no mail server is turned on, a change needs a restart, or the activity log has errors from the last day.

The menu on the left groups the same sections. Within a section, settings are grouped into cards, with rarely needed options behind Advanced. On a phone, the overview's cards are the menu, and each section links back to them.

docs.title: Mail servers
docs.text: The mail servers that send your email. You can add several, and listnun spreads sending across the enabled ones. Use Test connection after changing one.

docs.title: Sending speed
docs.text: How fast campaigns send: how many messages go out at once, a rate limit per second, and an optional sliding window (at most N messages per period) to stay within your mail provider's limits. Leave these alone unless your provider asks you to send more slowly.

docs.title: Other channels
docs.text: Optional extra ways to send, such as SMS, through HTTP webhooks ("postback" messengers). See Messengers.

docs.title: Bounces and complaints
docs.text: What happens when an email bounces (nothing, unsubscribe, blocklist or delete, separately for hard and soft bounces and complaints), and how bounces reach listnun: from your provider's webhooks (Amazon SES, SendGrid, Postmark and others) or by checking a bounce mailbox. See Bounce processing.

docs.title: Inactive subscribers
docs.text:
Subscribers who never open or click hurt how often your emails reach inboxes. Inactive cleanup, under Inactive subscribers, deals with them on a schedule. It's off until you turn on Run inactive cleanup.

Run inactive cleanupOff by default. Nothing happens to subscribers until you turn this on. ManagedListnun sets and maintains the rules. Nothing to configure. CustomSet your own inactivity window, action and schedule. Managed rulesSet by Listnun Inactive forNo activity within this window180 days Counts as activityOpened or clicked ActionUnsubscribe from all lists RunsWeekly, Sunday 02:00 Next run Sun 26 Oct, 02:00About 640 subscribers match the managed rules today.Preview affected subscribers

Settings › Inactive subscribers in Managed mode.

Pick Managed to use listnun's recommended rules (shown read-only), or Custom to set your own:

Rule Options Inactive for No activity for 30 to 365 days. Counts as activity Opened, clicked, or either. Action Unsubscribe from all lists, blocklist, or delete. Delete can't be undone. Applies to All lists, or only some. Runs Daily, weekly or monthly, at 02:00.

To be safe, someone only counts as inactive if they joined the list before the window began and a campaign actually went to that list during it. Blocklisted subscribers are left alone.

The card at the bottom shows when it runs next and how many subscribers match today. Preview affected subscribers counts matches for the rules on screen, before you save.

Cleanup needs Individual subscriber tracking (in Privacy and consent) to be on. Without it, everyone would look inactive, so listnun won't run it and shows a warning.

docs.title: Email validation
docs.text: Checks your subscribers' email addresses with Scrub, so campaigns don't go to addresses that would bounce. You can validate a list on demand, and imports are checked in the background. While a list is being validated, campaigns to it can't start.

docs.title: Privacy and consent
docs.text: Setting What it does Individual subscriber tracking Records which subscriber opened or clicked. Off counts opens and clicks only in total. Inactive cleanup needs it on. Disable tracking Turns off open and click tracking completely. Include List-Unsubscribe header Lets email apps show their own unsubscribe button. Recommended. Allow blocklisting, preference changes, exporting, wiping What subscribers can do for themselves from the links in your emails. Record opt-in IP address Keeps the IP address people confirm their subscription from, as proof of consent. Domain blocklist / allowlist Refuse signups and imports from some email domains, or only accept certain ones.

docs.title: Sign-in and security
docs.text:
• Single sign-on (OIDC): let your team sign in with Google, Microsoft or another provider. See OIDC SSO.
  • Captcha: protect your signup forms, and optionally the sign-in page, with Cloudflare Turnstile.
  • Require two-step verification: everyone who signs in with a password must set up an authenticator app. See Your team.
  • Trusted redirect URLs: the addresses signup forms may send people to afterwards.

docs.title: Workspace
docs.text:
• Root URL, Site name, Logo URL and Favicon URL: your workspace's public address and branding on its public pages.
  • Default from email for new campaigns.
  • Admin notification e-mails: who gets told when, for example, an import or a campaign finishes.
  • Language of the app and the public pages.
  • Whether to show the public subscription page and the public mailing list archive (and whether its RSS feed has the full content).
  • Double opt-in behaviour: whether to send the confirmation email and show the confirmation page.

docs.title: Appearance
docs.text: Custom CSS and JavaScript for the admin app and for your public pages (signup, unsubscribe, archive).

docs.title: File storage
docs.text:
Where uploaded files are stored, which file types are allowed, and the maximum upload size.

  • Local filesystem keeps files on the listnun server.
  • S3-compatible uses any S3-style object storage: AWS S3, Hetzner Object Storage, Cloudflare R2, MinIO, RustFS and others. Set the Endpoint to the provider's S3 URL (for example https://fsn1.your-objectstorage.com for Hetzner), plus the region, bucket and access keys. A public bucket gives files plain links; a private one uses links that expire.

See Media storage for setting a bucket up.

docs.title: Data cleanup
docs.text:
Tidy-up jobs you run by hand. Each one asks you to confirm, and none can be undone.

  • Subscribers: delete orphans (subscribers on no list) or all blocklisted subscribers, with their activity.
  • Subscriptions: remove double opt-in subscriptions still unconfirmed after a date.
  • Analytics: delete view and click records before a date (campaign totals stay), or export them first.
  • Database: vacuum the database on a schedule to keep it fast.

docs.title: Activity log
docs.text:
Your workspace's recent activity: settings changes and who made them, campaigns starting, pausing and finishing, imports finishing, webhook retries and failures, inactive cleanup runs, and send failures. It shows the latest 500 lines and keeps 30 days. Turn on Auto-refresh to watch it live.

When email can't be sent, the log shows why, under the source sending. Each line starts with the likely cause (the mail server rejected the login, couldn't be reached, failed TLS, or refused the message) followed by the server's own error. A failing campaign logs its first error once per run, not once per email. Test sends are logged too, and the error is also shown to whoever sent the test.

docs.title: Subscribers
docs.text: Open Subscribers › All subscribers to see everyone in your workspace. Pick a segment on the left to narrow the table down, search by email or name, and click a subscriber to open their details on the right.

docs.title: A subscriber's details
docs.text:
The detail panel shows:

  • their email, name and status,
  • the lists they're on, and whether each subscription is confirmed, unconfirmed or unsubscribed,
  • their attributes: any extra data you keep about them, such as a city or a plan (see Concepts),
  • their activity: campaigns sent to them, opens, clicks and bounces.

From there you can edit them, change their lists, blocklist them or delete them.

docs.title: Statuses
docs.text:
A subscriber has one overall status:

Status Meaning Enabled Normal. They get campaigns for the lists they're on. Blocklisted They get nothing, whatever lists they're on. Used for people who asked never to be emailed, or addresses that keep bouncing.

Each list subscription has its own status too: Unconfirmed (double opt-in lists only: waiting for them to click the confirmation link), Confirmed, or Unsubscribed.

docs.title: Confirming someone yourself
docs.text:
If someone confirmed some other way, such as by replying or on the phone, you can confirm them yourself instead of waiting for them to click the link:

  • One person: open them, go to the Subscriptions tab and click Mark as confirmed next to the list.
  • Many people: select them, click Add to list, choose Mark as confirmed and pick the lists.

This only confirms subscriptions that are waiting. Unsubscribed people stay unsubscribed, so you can't re-subscribe someone by accident, and nobody gets added to a list they weren't on.

docs.title: Segments
docs.text:
A segment is a group of subscribers who match some conditions, such as "lives in Harare and joined in the last 90 days". The Segments column on the left of Subscribers has built-in ones:

Segment Who's in it Everyone All subscribers. Engaged Opened a campaign in the last 90 days. New this month Joined in the last 30 days. Never opened Have never opened a campaign. Not confirmed yet Have at least one double opt-in subscription waiting for confirmation. Blocklisted Blocklisted subscribers.

Below them, under Saved by your team, are the segments your team saved.

docs.title: Building a segment
docs.text:
Click New segment (or change the conditions of any segment) and choose whether people must match all or any of the conditions. Each condition is a field, a test and usually a value:

Field Tests Attribute (enter its name, e.g. city) is, is not, contains, is set Email, Name is, is not, contains, is set Joined in the last / not in the last N days, before / after a date On list is, is not (unsubscribed people don't count as on the list) Status is, is not: enabled or blocklisted Waiting to confirm is Last opened, Last clicked in the last / not in the last N days, before / after a date, never

The table and the count above it update as you edit. A segment can have up to 20 conditions. Click Save segment to give it a name and keep it for your team; Delete segment removes a saved segment but not the people in it. Saving and deleting segments needs the subscribers:manage permission.

docs.title: Using a segment
docs.text:
Whatever segment you're viewing also limits:

  • select all: ticking the header checkbox selects everyone in the segment, not everyone in the workspace,
  • the bulk actions on that selection (add to or remove from lists, unsubscribe, blocklist, delete),
  • Export, which downloads only the people in the segment.

docs.title: Edit as SQL
docs.text: If you have the subscribers:sql_query permission, Edit as SQL turns the segment's conditions into an SQL expression in the advanced search box, for cases the builder can't express. See Querying and segmenting subscribers. Segments themselves don't need that permission.

docs.title: Working with many at once
docs.text: Tick subscribers (or use the header checkbox to select everyone in the current segment and search) and the action bar appears above the table. You can add them to lists, remove them from lists, mark their subscriptions confirmed or unsubscribed, blocklist or delete them.

docs.title: Bounces
docs.text:
When an email can't be delivered, the mail provider reports a bounce. Subscribers › Bounces lists them, filtered by type:

Type Meaning Hard The address doesn't exist or permanently refuses mail. Soft A temporary problem, such as a full mailbox. Complaint The person marked your email as spam.

Search by email or campaign, and filter by type, campaign or source. Click a bounce to see what the provider reported: its type, description and the mail server's reply.

Select bounces to Delete the records or Blocklist the subscribers behind them. Delete all and selecting everything act on exactly what the list shows, so with a filter or search on, only the matching bounces are affected. Deleting bounce records doesn't change the subscribers.

Bounces are only recorded for subscribers. A bounce for an address that isn't one, such as a transactional email to a non-subscriber or a subscriber you've since deleted, is skipped.

What happens after a bounce (nothing, unsubscribe, blocklist or delete) is set in Settings › Bounces and complaints. See Bounce processing for how bounces reach listnun.

docs.title: Inactive subscribers
docs.text: People who never open or click hurt how often your emails reach the inbox. Settings › Inactive subscribers can tidy them up on a schedule. See Settings.

docs.title: Your team
docs.text:
Open Workspace › Team to manage who can use your workspace and what they can do. It has three tabs: Members, Roles and List access.

To connect another system to listnun, don't add a member. Create an API key instead. API users made before API keys existed are listed, and can be migrated, under Developers › API keys.

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
The table shows each member's role, whether they use two-step verification, and when they were last active. Members who sign in with single sign-on show SSO under two-step, since their identity provider handles it.

Add member creates a teammate:

Field Notes Username What they sign in with, when using a password. Name and email Shown in the app and used for notifications. Enable password login Off means they sign in with single sign-on only (see OIDC SSO). User role What they can do across the workspace. List role Optionally, which lists they can see and manage. Status Deactivated members can't sign in.

To change someone's role, pick a new one from the picker on their row. Making someone a Super Admin asks you to confirm first. You can't change your own role, or a deactivated member's. Open a member to change anything else, or use their row's menu to Deactivate them.

Deactivated members are folded away under N deactivated accounts below the table. Searching still finds them.

If any active members sign in with just a password and no two-step verification, a banner says how many and links to Require two-step for everyone. See Requiring it for everyone.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text: A user role is a set of permissions, such as "can send campaigns" or "can manage settings". The built-in Super Admin role can do everything. Create roles for the jobs people do, such as an Editor who writes campaigns but can't change settings. See Roles and permissions for the full list of permissions.

docs.title: List access
docs.text:
A list role limits a user to particular lists: for each list, whether they can see its subscribers and whether they can manage them. Give it to users who should only work with some of your lists. A user role with lists:get_all or lists:manage_all overrides it.

Deleting a list role doesn't delete the users who had it; they just lose its list access.

docs.title: Your profile and two-step verification
docs.text:
Click your initials at the top right and choose Profile.

  • Details: change your name and email. If you sign in with single sign-on, your email comes from your provider and can't be changed here.
  • Password: enter your current password, then the new one twice (at least 8 characters). Changing it signs you out everywhere else.
  • Two-factor authentication: click Turn on, scan the QR code with an authenticator app (such as Ente Auth or Google Authenticator), and enter the 6-digit code it shows. From then on you'll be asked for a code each time you sign in. To turn it off, enter your password.

docs.title: Requiring it for everyone
docs.text: An admin can turn on Settings › Sign-in and security › Require two-step verification. People who sign in with a password then have to set it up before they can use the workspace: they're taken to their profile with a note explaining why. Single sign-on users and API keys aren't affected.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
A template is the layout around a campaign's content: the header, footer, styles and unsubscribe link. Open Campaigns › Templates to see them as cards with a preview, filtered by type:

Type Used for Campaign / HTML Rich text, Raw HTML, Markdown and Plain text campaigns. The campaign's content is placed into the template. Campaign / Visual A starting design for Visual campaigns. Importing one copies its blocks into the campaign, which you then edit freely. Transactional Transactional emails sent through the API. These are edited under Developers › Email templates. See Transactional email.

One campaign template is the Default: new campaigns use it unless you pick another. Set it from a template's ⋯ menu, where you can also clone and delete templates. The default template can't be deleted; make another one the default first.

docs.title: Writing an HTML template
docs.text:
An HTML campaign template is a full HTML email with one required line where the campaign's content goes:

{{ template "content" . }}

Templates use the listmonk template language, so you can add the subscriber's name, unsubscribe link and so on. Include these two so your emails work properly:

  • {{ UnsubscribeURL }}: the unsubscribe link. Every bulk email should have one.
  • {{ TrackView }}: the invisible image that counts opens. Without it, opens aren't counted for campaigns using this template.

See the Templating reference for everything you can use. Preview shows the template with sample content and a sample subscriber.

docs.title: Visual template width
docs.text: A visual email is 600px wide unless you change it. Click the area around the email in the builder to open its Global settings, and set Content width anywhere from 480px to 800px. Campaigns imported from the template take its width, and each campaign can change its own. On phones the email still shrinks to fit the screen. With Outlook compatibility on, Outlook on Windows keeps to the width too.

docs.title: Media
docs.text:
Campaigns › Media is your workspace's library of images and files, used for images in campaigns, campaign attachments and your email logo.

  • Drop files on the upload area, or click to choose them. Uploads over your workspace's size limit (set in Settings › File storage) are refused.
  • Click a file to open it. Tick files to delete several at once.
  • The storage panel shows how much space your files use.

Files are stored wherever your workspace is set up to keep them: on the server, or in S3-compatible storage. See Settings.

docs.title: Tracking opens and clicks
docs.text:
listnun can tell you who opened a campaign and which links they clicked, and, where it's set up, who replied (Replies). You set it up per campaign in the Tracking card on the Content step. Nothing needs adding to the email by hand.

Tracking Track link clicksCounts who clicks each link, in every editor. No codes to add. Tracking pixels https://www.facebook.com/tr?id=123&ev=PageView&noscript=1✕ Paste a pixel link, or the <img> code from Meta, Google Ads, LinkedIn…Add pixel For ad and analytics platforms that count opens with an image. Many email apps block images until the reader allows them, so these counts run low.

The Tracking card on a campaign's Content step, with one pixel added.

docs.title: Track link clicks
docs.text:
With Track link clicks on, every web link in the email is tracked: when someone clicks, listnun counts it and sends them on to the real address. It works the same in every format, including Visual, Rich text, Raw HTML and Markdown.

It's on by default for new campaigns. Campaigns created before this switch existed start with it off, so they keep sending exactly as before; turn it on if you want clicks counted.

Some links are never rewritten:

  • unsubscribe, preferences and view-in-browser links (listnun handles these itself),
  • mailto: and other non-web links,
  • links that are already tracked,
  • links containing a template expression, such as https://example.com/{{ .Subscriber.UUID }}.

Tracking applies to HTML emails. Plain-text campaigns, and the plain-text version of an HTML campaign, aren't tracked.

Tracking a single link by hand

In Raw HTML or Markdown you can still track one link without the switch by adding @TrackLink to its address: https://example.com@TrackLink. In Rich text, tick Track link in the link dialog. See the Templating reference.

docs.title: Tracking pixels
docs.text:
Ad and analytics platforms, such as Meta, Google Ads and LinkedIn, can count email opens with a tiny invisible image called a pixel. To add one:

  1. In the platform, find the pixel's image address, or the <img …> code it gives you.
  2. Paste either into Tracking pixels and click Add pixel.

If you paste a whole snippet, listnun pulls out the image address, including from inside <noscript>. If the snippet is only a <script>, listnun explains that scripts don't run in email. Look for the image (noscript) version instead.

Pixel addresses must start with https:// (or http://). You can add up to 10 per campaign, and remove one with its ×. Pixels go at the end of the email and are added to every subscriber's copy.

docs.title: Open tracking
docs.text: listnun counts opens with its own tracking image, which the default templates include as {{ TrackView }}. If you write your own template, include it to count opens. See Templates.

docs.title: Why the numbers aren't exact
docs.text:
• Many email apps block images until the reader allows them, and some load every image automatically to protect privacy. Open counts (yours and any pixel's) are therefore approximate. Clicks are reliable.
  • If Settings › Privacy and consent › Individual subscriber tracking is off, listnun counts opens and clicks in total but not per subscriber.
  • If Disable tracking is on in Settings › Privacy and consent, nothing is tracked at all, whatever the campaign says.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
listnun is built to be highly performant and can handle millions of subscribers with minimal system resources.

However, as the Postgres database grows—with a large number of subscribers, campaign views, and click records—it can significantly slow down certain aspects of the program, particularly in counting records and aggregating various statistics. For instance, loading admin pages that do these aggregations can take tens of seconds if the database has millions of subscribers.

  • Aggregate counts, statistics, and charts on the landing dashboard.
  • Subscriber count beside every list on the Lists page.
  • Total subscriber count on the Subscribers page.

However, at that scale, viewing the exact number of subscribers or statistics every time the admin panel is accessed becomes mostly unnecessary. On installations with millions of subscribers, where the above pages do not load instantly, it is highly recommended to turn on the Settings -> Performance -> Cache slow database queries option.

docs.title: Slow query caching
docs.text: When this option is enabled, the subscriber counts on the Lists page, the Subscribers page, and the statistics on the dashboard, etc., are no longer counted in real-time in the database. Instead, they are updated periodically and cached, resulting in a massive performance boost. The periodicity can be configured on the Settings -> Performance page using a standard crontab expression (default: 0 3 * * *, which means 3 AM daily). Use a tool like crontab.guru for easily generating a desired crontab expression.

docs.title: VACUUM-ing
docs.text: Running VACUUM ANALYZE on large Postgres databases at regular intervals (for instance, once a week), is recommended. It reclaims disk space and improves Postgres' query performance. Do note that this is a blocking operation and all database queries can come to a stand-still on a large database while the operation is running (generally only a few seconds).

docs.title: Media storage
docs.text: Uploaded media (campaign images, attachments, logos) is stored either on the listnun server's disk or in S3-compatible object storage. Each workspace chooses in Settings › File storage.

docs.title: Local filesystem
docs.text:
Files go in the upload path on the server (default uploads, relative to the working directory) and are served from the upload URI (default /uploads). With Docker, mount that path on a volume so uploads survive container rebuilds. See Configuration.

The filesystem only works for a single server. Use S3-compatible storage if you run more than one, or host many workspaces.

docs.title: S3-compatible storage
docs.text:
Any service that speaks the S3 API works: AWS S3, Hetzner Object Storage, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, MinIO, RustFS, Garage and others.

Setting Value Endpoint The provider's S3 URL, e.g. https://fsn1.your-objectstorage.com (Hetzner) or https://s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com (AWS). Region The bucket's region, e.g. eu-central, or us-east-1 for most self-hosted stores. Bucket The bucket name. Bucket path A folder inside the bucket, or / for the root. Access key / Secret Credentials that can read and write the bucket. Bucket type Public: files get plain links. Private: links are signed and expire after the expiry you set. Public URL Optional, e.g. a CDN or custom domain in front of the bucket. Links use it instead of the endpoint.

listnun uses path-style addresses (endpoint/bucket/file), which every S3-compatible store supports.

docs.title: Public buckets
docs.text:
For a public bucket, links in emails must open for anyone. listnun marks uploads public-read, but many S3-compatible stores (MinIO, RustFS and others) ignore per-file permissions. Give the bucket a policy that lets anyone read objects instead:

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Principal": {"AWS": ["*"]},
    "Action": ["s3:GetObject"],
    "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::listnun-media/*"]
  }]
}

Only reading is public. Uploading and deleting still need the access key.

docs.title: Trying it locally with RustFS
docs.text:
RustFS is a small S3-compatible server, handy for development:

docker run -d --name listnun-s3 --restart unless-stopped \
  -p 127.0.0.1:9200:9000 -p 127.0.0.1:9201:9001 \
  -v listnun-s3-data:/data \
  -e RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY=listnun -e RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY=listnun-secret \
  -e RUSTFS_CONSOLE_ENABLE=true \
  rustfs/rustfs:1.0.1

Create a bucket in the console at http://127.0.0.1:9201 (or with any S3 client) and give it the policy above. Then in Settings › File storage, choose S3-compatible with endpoint http://127.0.0.1:9200, region us-east-1, your bucket, and the keys. Links will be local, so images won't load in emails opened on other devices.

docs.title: Storage use
docs.text: listnun records each file's size. Workspaces see their total on the Media page, and the operator API reports it per workspace at GET /api/operator/tenants/:id/storage.

docs.title: Workspaces and the operator API
docs.text:
One listnun instance can host many workspaces (tenants). Each has its own subscribers, campaigns, users and settings, isolated in the database by Postgres row-level security. Workspaces are created and managed through the operator API, not the admin app.

A plain self-hosted install doesn't need any of this. With multi-tenancy off (the default), everything belongs to a single workspace.

docs.title: Turning on multi-tenancy
docs.text:
[app]
multi_tenancy_enabled = true
root_domain = "listnun.example.com"

# Where suspended workspaces' admin UI redirects to (optional).
console_url = "https://console.example.com"

Every request must then arrive on a workspace's own host:

  • <slug>.listnun.example.com, from the workspace's slug, or
  • the workspace's custom domain, if one is set.

Requests for unknown hosts are rejected. Suspended or disabled workspaces show a "workspace unavailable" page: their public pages and API return 503, and their admin app redirects to console_url when it's set.

You'll need a wildcard DNS record (*.listnun.example.com) and a wildcard TLS certificate, for example from Let's Encrypt using the DNS-01 challenge.

Sessions and API keys belong to one workspace. A session cookie or key from one workspace is refused on another's host.

Links listnun generates use the host the request came in on, so each workspace's links point at its own address: password-reset emails, signup forms' hosted pages, embed code and popup scripts, and the archive feed. The root_url setting is only used for single-workspace installs. If a workspace has a custom domain, open its admin app on that domain to get links on it.

Testing locally

Browsers resolve *.localhost to your machine, so acme.localhost:9000 works for reading pages. Signing in through the browser needs a real domain, though; an /etc/hosts entry isn't enough.

docs.title: The operator API
docs.text:
The operator API is a separate, cross-workspace API under /api/operator, for provisioning and billing systems. It's off until you set a token:

[operator]
token = "a-long-random-secret"

# A separate Postgres role with BYPASSRLS, for reading across workspaces.
db_user = "listnun_operator"
db_password = "…"

# "dev" makes generated workspace URLs <slug>-dev.<root_domain>, so a dev
# and a prod instance can share a root domain. Empty for prod.
env = ""

Authenticate with the token as a bearer token:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer a-long-random-secret" https://listnun.example.com/api/operator/tenants

Warning

The operator token can create and delete any workspace. Keep it in your secrets manager, never in a browser. Use a dedicated Postgres role with BYPASSRLS for db_user; the app's own role must never have it, or row-level security stops protecting workspaces from each other.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Endpoint Does GET /api/operator/tenants List workspaces, with status and user and subscriber counts. GET /api/operator/tenants/:id One workspace. POST /api/operator/tenants Create a workspace (slug, name, first admin, optional organization). Returns a one-time setup link for the admin to set their own password. POST /api/operator/tenants/:id/setup-link Issue a fresh setup link. Links expire after 7 days, work once, and only last as long as the server process, so reissue after a restart. GET /api/operator/tenants/:id/setup-link?token=&email= Check a setup link without using it up: {"valid": …, "password_set": …}. valid is whether it still works for that admin; password_set is whether the admin has a password, meaning the link was used. Doesn't count towards the link's attempt limit. PUT /api/operator/tenants/:id/status Suspend, reactivate or disable: {"status": "suspended"}. Suspended workspaces don't send campaigns. DELETE /api/operator/tenants/:id Permanently delete a workspace and all its data. Workspace 1 can't be deleted. PUT /api/operator/tenants/:id/smtp Set the workspace's SMTP server. It's used from the next send. PUT /api/operator/tenants/:id/from-email Set the workspace's default From address, which new campaigns start with: {"from_email": "Acme <news@acme.com>"} or a bare address. New workspaces start with a placeholder that can't send, so set this once a real sending address is verified. The workspace can still change it in its settings. PUT /api/operator/tenants/:id/scrub Configure email validation (Scrub) for the workspace. GET /api/operator/tenants/:id/scrub/usage The workspace's validation usage. PUT /api/operator/tenants/:id/bounce-webhooks Configure bounce webhooks for the workspace's mail provider. PUT /api/operator/tenants/:id/replies Set up reply tracking for the workspace. PUT /api/operator/tenants/:id/custom-domain Set or clear the workspace's custom domain. GET /api/operator/tenants/:id/storage Media storage the workspace uses. GET /api/operator/tenants/:id/usage Emails sent and validations over ?from=&to= (RFC 3339), optionally &group=day. GET /api/operator/usage The same for every workspace at once, plus a daily series. GET /api/operator/tenants/:id/activity The workspace's latest activity log lines (its Settings › Activity log). ?source=sending returns only send failures; ?limit= up to 500. GET /api/operator/tenants/:id/sending-health Campaign email sent, hard bounces and spam complaints over the last 30 days, rated against Gmail's limits the same way as the campaign inbox check, plus the workspace's unsent campaigns that have no unsubscribe link and so can't start. GET POST DELETE /api/operator/organizations… Group workspaces by customer. Deleting an organization detaches its workspaces; it doesn't delete them.

The full request and response shapes are in the OpenAPI spec at /api/swagger/index.html, under operator.

docs.title: Reply tracking
docs.text:
Campaign reply tracking uses each workspace's own Postmark server and its inbound stream. To turn it on for a workspace, send its setup:

curl -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer a-long-random-secret" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://listnun.example.com/api/operator/tenants/42/replies \
  -d '{
    "inbound_address": "abc123@inbound.postmarkapp.com",
    "secret": "at-least-16-characters",
    "webhook_username": "replies",
    "webhook_password": "…"
  }'
Field Notes inbound_address The Postmark server's inbound address, or the same local part on a reply domain. Each email's Reply-To adds a token to it (<local>+<token>@<domain>). Empty turns reply tracking off for the workspace. secret Signs the reply tokens, at least 16 characters. Keep it stable: changing it orphans replies to emails already sent. webhook_username, webhook_password The basic-auth credentials Postmark sends with each inbound webhook.

Then point the Postmark server's inbound webhook at https://<workspace host>/webhooks/replies/postmark with the same credentials. A reply is only accepted if it arrives at an address with that workspace's inbound local part and a token signed by its secret. The domain isn't checked, so the address can move to a reply domain without breaking replies to emails already sent. The setup is stored apart from the workspace's settings, so the workspace's admins can't see or change it, and the Track replies switch only appears in its campaigns once it's set.

docs.title: Reply domains
docs.text:
Reply addresses can use the workspace's own domain instead of inbound.postmarkapp.com:

  1. The workspace publishes an MX record for a subdomain it uses only for replies: reply.acme.com MX 10 inbound.postmarkapp.com. Not its main domain: that MX would send all of its own mail to Postmark.
  2. Set that domain as the Postmark server's inbound domain (InboundDomain on PUT /servers/{id}). Postmark lets an inbound domain belong to only one server.
  3. Send the replies setup again with inbound_address set to the server's inbound local part on the new domain, e.g. abc123@reply.acme.com, and the same secret.

Keeping the local part means replies to emails sent before the switch, addressed to abc123+<token>@inbound.postmarkapp.com, still match. To undo it, send the setup with the original address first, then clear the server's inbound domain, so no new email carries an address Postmark no longer accepts.

On hosted listnun, the console does all of this from the workspace page's Reply domain section.

docs.title: Usage for billing
docs.text: listnun counts each workspace's billable usage when it happens: every email sent through an SMTP messenger (one per recipient), and every address submitted for validation. Counts are kept per hour. A from/to window counts each hour once, so back-to-back billing periods never double-count. A deleted workspace's usage stays available, so it can still be invoiced.

docs.title: Quickstart: send your first campaign
docs.text: This walks you from an empty workspace to a sent campaign in about ten minutes. You'll need a CSV file of subscribers, or you can add a few by hand.

docs.title: 1. Create a list
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, open Lists › All lists and click New list.
  2. Give it a name, for example Newsletter.
  3. Choose who can see it:
    • Public lists appear on your subscription forms, so people can join them.
    • Private lists are only for you; people can't sign up to them.
  4. Choose the opt-in:
    • Single opt-in adds people straight away.
    • Double opt-in emails each new subscriber a confirmation link first, and campaigns only go to people who confirmed.
  5. Click Save.

docs.title: 2. Add subscribers
docs.text:
To bring in many at once, open Subscribers › Import:

  1. Drop your CSV file on the upload area (a ZIP containing a CSV also works).
  2. Under Options, choose Subscribe, pick your list, and set the subscription status.
  3. Click Import. A progress bar shows the import as it runs, then how many were imported, skipped and failed.

Your CSV needs an email column. A name column and an attributes column (JSON) are optional. See Importing subscribers for the full format.

To add one person, open Subscribers › All subscribers and click New subscriber.

docs.title: 3. Write the campaign
docs.text:
Open Campaigns › Create new. The editor has four steps along the top.

  1. Settings: give the campaign a name (only you see it), the subject line, the From address, and the lists to send to. Click Continue.
  2. Content: pick a format and write the email. Visual lets you build it from blocks; Rich text is a normal word-processor editor. Track link clicks is on by default, so you'll see who clicks each link. See Writing campaigns.
  3. Schedule: send as soon as you start it, or pick Schedule for later and a date and time.
  4. Review: a checklist of everything that matters before sending.

docs.title: 4. Send yourself a test
docs.text:
On the Review step, the Test email check stays amber until you send a test of the current version. Click Send test, enter your own email address, and check the email in your inbox: the layout, the links and how it looks on your phone.

If you change the subject or content after testing, the check turns amber again so you test the new version.

docs.title: 5. Start it
docs.text: Click Start campaign (or Schedule if you chose a time). listnun confirms how many subscribers it goes to, then starts sending. You can pause a running campaign from the campaigns list.

docs.title: 6. See the results
docs.text: Open Campaigns › Analytics, or the campaign in All campaigns, to see opens, clicks, bounces and which links people clicked.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:

docs.title: Signing in
docs.text:
Your workspace has its own address, such as https://yourcompany.listnun.app/admin. Sign in with your username and password, or with single sign-on if your workspace uses it. You can pick the language at the bottom of the sign-in page.

If your workspace requires two-step verification and you haven't set it up yet, you'll be taken to your profile to set it up before anything else. See Your profile and two-step verification.

Section What's in it Dashboard Subscriber growth, recent campaigns and activity for the period you choose. Lists All lists and Forms, where you build a signup form for your website. Subscribers All subscribers, Import and Bounces. Campaigns All campaigns, Create new, Media, Templates and Analytics. Developers API keys, email templates, send test, message log, email branding and webhooks. See Developers. Workspace Users (your team and their roles) and Settings.

Click a section with an arrow to open or close it. listnun remembers which sections you left open.

At the bottom, Collapse shrinks the sidebar to a narrow strip of icons to give your work more room; Expand brings it back. That's remembered too. Billing and workspace opens the listnun console, where you manage your plan.

docs.title: The top bar
docs.text:
• The breadcrumb shows where you are.
  • Refresh reloads the data on the page without reloading the whole app.
  • The moon and sun icon switches between dark and light mode.
  • Your initials open the account menu: your profile and signing out.

docs.text: On a narrow screen the sidebar becomes a menu behind the menu button at the top left.
